headline: On-policy distillation improves reported reasoning retention at sub-3-bit weights
summary: A September 2026 preprint studies why quantization-aware distillation can preserve short-form answers yet leave long mathematical and code generations impaired at sub-3-bit weight precision. The authors add on-policy distillation (OPD), which samples through the deployment quantized path and applies teacher guidance to the student's own generated prefixes, alongside task verifiers. Across Qwen3 and Falcon3 models at 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, they report higher math and code benchmark performance than the QAD starting checkpoints, including gains over a matched-budget continued-QAD control in all 16 reported comparisons. The released QAOPD repository links checkpoints and reproduction instructions. These remain author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction is open. The paper also reports a material implementation caveat: OPD uses a 16-bit KV cache in the principal arms rather than the released 8-bit KV-cache configuration, a deviation the authors say favors their results.
